ModuleEnabled.Name: Enable Dual Class
ModuleEnabled.Hint: Turn on the Dual-Class Characters variant rule. Every character then needs two classes: players cannot level one past 1st until it has both, though you can as GM.

TripleClass.Name: Allow a Third Class
TripleClass.Hint: Let every character take a third class, treated exactly like the second: the best of the three proficiencies, the highest Hit Points, the largest skill count rather than the sum, and a class feat ladder each. Not a published variant rule. To allow it for particular characters instead, leave this off and use Third Class Permissions.

ThirdClassPermissions.Name: Third Class Permissions
ThirdClassPermissions.Hint: Allow a third class to particular characters, for a world that is otherwise dual class. Ignored while Allow a Third Class is on, which already covers everyone.
ThirdClassPermissions.Label: Choose Characters
ThirdClassPermissions.Title: Third Class Permissions
ThirdClassPermissions.None: This world has no characters yet.
ThirdClassPermissions.TableHint: Ticked characters may take a third class. Unticking one does not remove a class they already have.

AncestryParagon.Name: Enable Ancestry Paragon
AncestryParagon.Hint: Every character gains a second ancestry feat at 1st level and another at each odd level thereafter, eleven in total. Independent of Dual Class. Skipped if another module already provides these slots.

Sheet.PickHint: The class keeps its own feat ladder, class DC and key attribute boost. Its features are granted straight away, so expect the usual choice prompts.
Sheet.NoClassesFound: No other class items were found in this world or its compendia.
Sheet.PrimaryIs: Primary class: {class}. The primary sets the character's key attribute and main class DC.
Sheet.Removed: Removed {class} and the features it granted.

Mismatch.Warning: {feat} is a {belongs} feat but was placed in the {placed} feat slots. It still counts; move it if that was not intended.

Skills.AllTrained: {actual} of {total} skills trained - all of them
Skills.AllTrainedWhy: Something on this character trains every skill, so the class skill picks have nothing left to spend on and there is no count worth showing.
Skills.LevelOneOnly: Shown at 1st level only, while every trained skill can still be traced back to where it came from.

Coexist.KeptFirstClass: {actor} kept {class} as its first class. Remove a class from the items list if you meant to replace it rather than add one.
Coexist.UnarmedManyClasses: {actor} already has {count} classes, so adding another replaces them. This module only handles two.

LevelGate.Blocked: Add the missing class before levelling past 1st: its 1st-level features and proficiencies belong to the character from the start.
LevelGate.GmAllowed: Levelling anyway because you are the GM.
